patterns.name: Composition effect
patterns.definition: An aggregate changes because the mix of its parts changed, not because any part changed.
patterns.mechanism: The aggregate is an average over groups with different levels; a shift in group shares moves the average.

patterns.name: Simpson's paradox
patterns.definition: A trend within every subgroup runs opposite to the trend in the pooled data.
patterns.mechanism: Group sizes differ, so the pooled comparison is dominated by a different group mix at each level.

patterns.name: Omitted confounders
patterns.definition: A raw association between group membership and an outcome is presented without the variables that explain it.
patterns.mechanism: The groups differ systematically in a third variable that also drives the outcome, so the association is not an effect of group membership.

patterns.name: Base-rate neglect
patterns.definition: A rate or share is read without the denominator or the base rate that produces it.
patterns.mechanism: The same absolute number implies very different rates depending on the population it is divided by.

patterns.name: Ecological fallacy
patterns.definition: A conclusion about individuals is drawn from data about regions or groups.
patterns.mechanism: An association between regional aggregates does not transfer to the individuals inside those regions.

patterns.name: Cherry-picking
patterns.definition: A single favourable figure is presented while other available figures point the other way.
patterns.mechanism: Selection of the time window, the subgroup or the indicator determines the result.

patterns.name: False causality
patterns.definition: A correlation is presented as a causal mechanism without a design that could support it.
patterns.mechanism: No identification strategy, no temporal ordering and no control group are offered for a causal claim.

patterns.name: Scapegoating
patterns.definition: A problem explained largely by other factors is attributed to the presence or behaviour of a group.
patterns.mechanism: An outcome driven by structure is reattributed to a group's identity, which shifts blame onto that group without an evidential basis.

patterns.name: Moving the goalposts
patterns.definition: After a claim is addressed, the standard of proof or the claim itself shifts.
patterns.mechanism: Each answer is met with a new requirement, so no evidence could ever settle the question.
